checkpoints.description: [1/2] Review the last 63 pushes: keep siblings when a negation points at an unignored directory

impact_assessment.why: find_python_files treats every top-level directory named by a negation as a kept directory, so '!/pkg/keep.py' under the normal pkg/ drops pkg/mod.py from the code map even though git tracks it.
impact_assessment.benefits: The sibling filter applies only to directories the root .gitignore actually excludes; a normal directory keeps all of its Python files.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Python discovery walk; dependency: stdlib; concurrency: none; state: update_knowledge_base.py, tests, ADR, map
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first discovery test, existing negation and wildcard tests, unit tier, root scan, reachability and secret gates

[1/2] Review the last 66 pushes: skip HTML comments and rules when finding the README description

impact_assessment.why: extract_readme_description and update_readme_for_archive treat a multi-line HTML comment or an underscore rule as the first prose block; the archived repo then gets a comment fragment or '___' as its description and the banner lands before the real summary.
impact_assessment.benefits: Comment blocks and thematic breaks are skipped as non-prose, so the GitHub description and banner position use the actual tagline.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: README description and archive banner; dependency: stdlib re; concurrency: none; state: project_publish.py, project_archive.py, tests, ADR, map
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first multi-line-comment and rule tests, existing archive tests, unit tier, root scan, reachability and secret gates
